nodes.title: Model Files — Full BF16 Krea 2 Turbo
widgets_values:
## This workflow uses your full BF16 model

**Diffusion model**

- `krea2_turbo_bf16.safetensors`
- Original download: [krea/Krea-2-Turbo — turbo.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/krea/Krea-2-Turbo/resolve/main/turbo.safetensors)
- Location: `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/`
- This is the large BF16 model, not the Comfy-Org INT8 ConvRot model.

**Text encoder**

- `qwen3vl_4b_fp8_scaled.safetensors`
- Location: `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/`

**VAE**

- `qwen_image_vae.safetensors`
- Location: `ComfyUI/models/vae/`

**LoRA**

- `snofsKreaV13D.j1nF.safetensors`
- Location: `ComfyUI/models/loras/`

The four file selectors are visible on the main subgraph node and inside the subgraph. Double-click the subgraph to inspect the complete pipeline.

The BF16 diffusion model is approximately 24.5 GiB and may require substantial system-RAM offloading on an 8 GiB GPU.

nodes.title: Masked editing instructions
widgets_values:
## Optimized Krea 2 masked editing

The **white** mask area is editable; black is protected. The main prompt describes the complete photograph.

Visible controls currently include the main seed, denoise, mask growth, LoRA and mask feathering, plus the optional skin-colour post-pass:
- `PostSkinPassControl`: enable or bypass the second sampler
- `PostSkinDenoise`: start at `0.50`; try `0.40–0.60`
- `PostSkinPrompt`: tells Krea to preserve the garment while matching new skin to visible face, neck, arms and hands

The post-pass starts from the first-pass image, uses the same soft mask and Differential Diffusion model, then composites only through that mask. When disabled, its lazy switch prevents the second sampler from running.

Download the style LoRAs used in this workflow from [Comfy-Org/Krea-2/loras](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Krea-2/tree/main/loras). Place the `.safetensors` files in `ComfyUI/models/loras/`.

| LoRA                   | Trigger Words                        | Recommended Strength |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------|-------|
| `krea2_darkbrush`      | `monochrome ink wash style`          | `1.0` |
| `krea2_dotmatrix`      | `monochrome stippling style`         | `1.0` |
| `krea2_kidsdrawing`    | `naive expressive sketch style`      | `1.0` |
| `krea2_neondrip`       | `textured abstract style`            | `1.0` |
| `krea2_rainywindow`    | `rainy window style`                 | `1.0` |
| `krea2_retroanime`     | `purple retro anime style`           | `1.0` |
| `krea2_softwatercolor` | `art deco watercolor style`          | `1.0` |
| `krea2_sunsetblur`     | `ethereal motion blur style`         | `1.0` |
| `krea2_vintagetarot`   | `vintage tarot style`                | `1.0` |

KREA-ONLY MASKED EDITING — QUICK START

1. Load the source and paint WHITE over the editable object.
2. Describe the COMPLETE photograph, including scene, lighting, texture and the desired replacement.
3. Tune the main denoise and mask growth for the size of the clothing change.
4. For inconsistent newly generated skin, enable PostSkinPassControl. Start PostSkinDenoise at 0.50 and adjust the visible PostSkinPrompt if necessary.

The optional post-pass re-encodes the first-pass result, reuses the same soft edit mask, and runs a lower-denoise skin-consistency prompt. OFF is a lazy bypass, so the second sampler is not executed. Because it reuses the clothing mask, it can subtly refine the garment as well as exposed skin.

nodes.title: Source image — right-click and open in Mask Editor
PostSkinPrompt
widgets_values: A full-body fashion photograph of the same person in the same pose, clothing and environment as the input. Preserve the garment and identity. Any exposed skin inside the editable region exactly matches the visible face, neck, arms and hands in complexion, undertone, exposure, highlights, shadows and natural skin texture. Realistic continuous skin transitions at clothing edges. Preserve anatomy, lighting, camera perspective and photographic grain.

A full-body fashion photograph of the same woman in the same pose and environment, wearing nothing from the waist up. Preserve her identity, face, hair, body proportions, and all existing exposed skin. Her skin retains exactly the same complexion, warm/cool undertone, exposure, highlights, and shadows as her face and arms in the source photograph.

A full-body fashion photograph of the same person in the same pose, clothing and environment as the input. Preserve the garment and identity. Any exposed skin inside the editable region exactly matches the visible face, neck, arms and hands in complexion, undertone, exposure, highlights, shadows and natural skin texture. Realistic continuous skin transitions at clothing edges. Preserve anatomy, lighting, camera perspective and photographic grain.

A high-resolution, surreal digital illustration showing a human hand holding a martini glass. The image is overlaid with whimsical, expressive ink-style doodles, including a cartoon figure inside the glass, a drawn citrus wedge on the rim, and various abstract sketches and faces surrounding the glass against a clean, white background. The style seamlessly blends a realistic, lit photograph with loose, hand-drawn marker artistry, creating a playful and artistic juxtaposition.
